papers.title: Lattice‐Defect‐Coordinated Microstructural Continuity and Mechanical Compatibility in LPBF‐Fabricated CoCrNi/316L Bimetallic Structures
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Bimetallic structures fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) provide an effective strategy for achieving multifunctional integration, yet interfacial structural continuity and the role of lattice defects remain insufficiently understood. In this work, a crack‐free CoCrNi/316L bimetallic structure was fabricated by LPBF, and its microstructural evolution and mechanical response were systematically investigated. A continuous single‐phase face‐centered cubic structure was maintained across the entire build without the formation of brittle intermetallic compounds. A pronounced gradient microstructure was observed along the building direction, where the CoCrNi end exhibited a high density of lattice defects, whereas the 316L end showed coarser grains and fewer defects. The CoCrNi/316L interface region was characterized by grain refinement, orientation dispersion, and a high density of coordinated lattice defects, mainly originating from remelting, compositional dilution, and enhanced re‐nucleation. This defect‐mediated microstructural hierarchy resulted in a continuous hardness gradient from ∼273 HV to ∼230 HV, with a stable intermediate region at the interface. The bimetallic structure achieved a balanced strength‐ductility combination, with fracture occurring in the 316L end rather than at the interface, indicating effective load transfer and deformation compatibility. These results suggest that the coordinated distribution of lattice defects, together with grain refinement, contributes to improved interfacial microstructural continuity and mechanical compatibility in LPBF‐fabricated CoCrNi/316L bimetallic structures, providing useful guidance for the design of high‐performance multi‐material components.

papers.title: Data-Driven Robust MPC for an Industrial Evaporator under Model Uncertainty and Sensor Degradation
papers.abstract: Model predictive control is attractive for industrial processes because constraints and multivariable interactions can be handled explicitly, but its performance depends on the credibility of the prediction model and the measurements supplied to the controller. This article develops a data-driven robust MPC framework for an industrial evaporator in which model uncertainty and sensor degradation are treated jointly. The open DaISy industrial evaporator benchmark (code 96-010) supplies the data basis: 6305 samples, three manipulated inputs and three measured outputs. Publicly reproducible system-identification results for this benchmark report a first experiment of 3300 samples, an order-eight prediction-error model, and five-step output mean-square errors of 0.0576, 0.1564 and 0.0193. These error scales are used to define relative residual uncertainty for a closed-loop benchmark-constrained surrogate. The controller combines a trust-weighted state estimate with scenario-based robust prediction across a finite uncertainty ensemble. Bias, drift, precision loss and dropout are injected into the sensor channels, and at the same time plant matrices are perturbed independently across Monte Carlo trials. In 200 composite-degradation scenarios with 12% plant-model uncertainty, the proposed robust MPC reduces mean normalized tracking RMSE from 0.2750 for nominal MPC to 0.2421, and reduces normalized performance-envelope exceedance from 14.12% to 6.02%. The improvement is obtained at a 6.75% increase in average control effort. The results show that a practical data-driven robust MPC architecture should not treat identification error and sensor integrity as separate problems; both must enter the online state estimate and the predictive optimization layer.

papers.title: XTRUDE: A Process‐Informed Framework for High‐Fidelity Analysis of Hydrogel Extrusion
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable extrusion of viscoelastic hydrogels is crucial for technologies ranging from 3D (bio)printing to injectable therapeutics, yet current methods to characterize extrusion performance fail to mimic key processing conditions. Consequently, extrusion performance cannot be precisely predicted or controlled, particularly for thermosensitive, shear‐thinning, or heterogeneous hydrogels. Fundamentally, reliable extrusion emerges from interactions between intrinsic material properties and extrinsic processing conditions. Here, we introduce XTRUDE (e XT rusion R heology for U nderstanding and D efining E xtrudability), a process‐informed characterization platform that recapitulates geometry‐specific and time‐dependent conditions of the extrusion process by integrating in situ pressure sensing, controlled thermal conditions, and process‐relevant flow‐path geometries. XTRUDE reveals extrusion‐specific phenomena inaccessible with conventional methods, including the process‐dependent evolution of apparent rheological response and time‐local instabilities such as heterogeneity‐induced variations in extrudate morphology. Across monolithic, thermosensitive, and granular hydrogel formulations, XTRUDE establishes temporal pressure fluctuation patterns as quantitative metrics to unravel mechanisms underlying extrusion variability and correlate pressure profiles with extrudate morphology. By linking intrinsic rheology with the extrusion environment, XTRUDE provides a quantitative, mechanistic framework to benchmark extrudability across soft matter systems. This framework enables reliable formulation development, reduces failure during process translation, and offers a generalizable tool for extrusion‐based technologies in biofabrication, therapeutic delivery, and soft material manufacturing.

papers.title: ASAS-NANP SYMPOSIUM: MATHEMATICAL MODELING IN ANIMAL NUTRITION: Model Transfer and Application in Livestock Production Systems
papers.abstract: Mathematical models have long supported nutrition management in livestock systems, progressing from early National Research Council empirical tables to complex mechanistic frameworks such as the Ruminant Nutrition System. What is less documented is how models are operationalized in commercial practice, particularly as data streams from precision livestock technologies, remote sensing, and other Internet of Things technologies are increasingly hybridized into existing modeling frameworks. A prevailing assumption is that greater sensing, automation, or algorithmic complexity will naturally translate into better decisions; however, adoption and impact in commercial systems remain uneven. To examine how models are actually used under real-world constraints, we conducted a literature review and semi-structured interviews (n = 11) with livestock producers, technology developers, consultants, and value-chain actors working at the interface of biology, data, models, and farm decision-making. Six cross-cutting themes emerged: 1) model augmentation of systems, 2) model predictive control (MPC), 3) human centered adoption, 4) technology fit, 5) data bottlenecks, and 6) data enlightened value chain (Figure 1). Collectively, these insights re-center nutrition as the integrating discipline for productivity, welfare, and sustainability, and emphasize MPC and open, interoperable data pipelines as prerequisites for moving beyond pilots toward durable adoption. Interviewees consistently emphasized that meaningful impact depends on aligning biological realism, software engineering, and value-chain incentives so that models support actionable decisions under commercial constraints, rather than pursuing automation for its own sake.

papers.title: Experimental Comparison of the Energy Absorption Properties of Different Cellular Materials
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Energy absorption under compressive load is a key criterion for the use of cellular materials in lightweight construction, protection, and damping applications. The choice of microstructure is essential, as it significantly influences the deformation behavior. For this reason, three structural classes of open‐celled materials are compared with each other. While open‐cell foam structures are characterized by a stochastically distributed cell geometry consisting of nodes and ligaments, beam‐based lattice structures are composed of regularly arranged unit cells. In contrast to both architectures, triply periodic minimal surface structures (TPMS) do not contain discrete nodes; they are formed by continuous, smooth, and periodic surfaces. To enable an objective comparison, open‐cell foams, TPMS, and conventional beam‐based lattice structures with identical relative density are produced using 3D printing and then experimentally examined under pressure loading. The differences in the resulting load‐deformation curves are presented in detail.

papers.title: A Weight‐Adaptive Ensemble Learning Method for Mapping Pine Caterpillar Infestation Risk in Northeast China Using Remote Sensing: Combining Dual Bayesian and Top‐k Strategies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Pine caterpillar ( Dendrolimus ) outbreaks pose serious threats to forest ecosystems and regional economies. Long‐term analysis of infestation risk is essential for early warning and prevention. This study developed a risk assessment method for Northeast China that addresses limitations in long‐term dependency and model generalization. A multi‐factor dataset was constructed by integrating snow, soil, and other habitat variables with historical outbreak sites. A Dual‐Bayesian optimized, Top‐k adaptive weighted blending model (DBO‐Tk‐AWEL) was proposed, achieving OA 94.16%, Recall 89.66%, F1‐score 93.24%, and AUC 97.42% for 2000–2024 risk assessment. Dual‐Bayesian optimization enables automated hyperparameter and weight tuning, improving robustness and generalization in complex, high‐dimensional, small‐sample tasks. Results indicate: (1) six major high‐risk areas—Changtu–Lingyuan, Dongfeng–Fushun, Antu, Daqingshan–Qing'an, Zhalantun–Horqin, and Mohe–Oroqen. (2) spatial expansion trending eastward and northward, with increasingly concentrated high‐risk zones. (3) risk levels peaking in 2017–2020 and declining to 1.02% by 2024. (4) strong forest‐type specificity, with Korean pine–Tilia amurensis forests dominating high‐risk areas, rising red pine risk, stable Pinus tabulaeformis , low‐risk Larix–Betula mixed forests, and increasing Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica risk since 2017. (5) SHAP analysis revealing quartic polynomial relationships between key factors and risk, with temperature, solar radiation, soil temperature, snow density, and depth positively influencing risk, and precipitation, runoff, and soil humidity negatively affecting it. This study provides a robust scientific basis for targeted early warning and ecological management of pine caterpillar risks in Northeast China.

papers.title: Coupled Heat and Mass Transfer on a Chilled Beer Bottle: Experimental Nu–Ra Correlation, Caputo Fractional‐Order Modeling, and Monte Carlo Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates coupled natural convection and vapor condensation on a chilled glass beer bottle exposed to warm humid air. A 600‐mL bottle initially at −1.5°C was monitored during warming at 19°C and 68% relative humidity. Experimentally derived temperature and condensate histories were used to estimate effective heat‐ and mass‐transfer coefficients and to obtain an empirical Nu–Ra relationship for the tested configuration. The resulting correlation, Nu = 11,717·Ra −0.371 (R 2 = 0.989), is restricted to the investigated transient cooled, humid, condensation‐active conditions. Classical and Caputo fractional‐order reduced models were compared to evaluate whether memory effects improved the description of the measured transients. The optimized fractional orders remained close to unity, and AIC favored the classical integer‐order model. Monte Carlo simulations showed low parametric uncertainty relative to measurement resolution. The framework provides experimentally grounded reduced‐order tools for analyzing coupled heat and mass transfer on chilled cylindrical surfaces while explicitly distinguishing parametric uncertainty from structural model limitations.

papers.title: The Implementation of Bloom's Taxonomy in Islamic Religious Education Learning During the Merdeka Curriculum Era: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: The implementation of Bloom’s Taxonomy has become increasingly important in Islamic Religious Education (Pendidikan Agama Islam / PAI) following the adoption of the Merdeka Curriculum, which emphasizes competency-based learning, character development, and Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS). However, previous studies have generally examined Bloom’s Taxonomy from limited perspectives, such as HOTS, assessment, learning models, or educational technology, while comprehensive reviews remain limited. This study aims to examine the application of Bloom’s Taxonomy in Islamic Religious Education instruction and identify significant trends related to the Merdeka Curriculum. Employing a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) methodology, this library research reviewed twelve journal articles published between 2025 and 2026, which were obtained through Google Scholar. The data were analyzed using thematic, comparative, and critical analysis approaches. The findings revealed four major trends. First, the cognitive domain was primarily implemented through HOTS-oriented learning, active learning, and problem-solving strategies. Second, the affective domain was developed through religious character education, value internalization, and affective assessment. Third, the psychomotor domain was strengthened through practice-based and experiential learning activities. Fourth, technology integration supported interactive learning, digital assessment, and the development of higher-order thinking skills. The study concludes that the effective implementation of Bloom’s Taxonomy in Islamic Religious Education requires the integration of cognitive, affective, psychomotor, and technological dimensions. This study contributes a conceptual framework that can support curriculum implementation, instructional design, and assessment practices in Islamic Religious Education within the Merdeka Curriculum context

papers.title: DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models increasingly rely on action experts that generate short action chunks under receding-horizon control. While chunk-level training is convenient across robot embodiments, it optimizes local action likelihood without explicitly accounting for long-horizon task success. Sequence-level reinforcement learning can address this limitation, but typically requires policy rollouts and closed-loop interaction, which are costly for real-robot manipulation. We introduce DriftOPD, a teacher-free, rollout-free framework for sequence-level on-policy distillation of continuous VLA action experts. We show that the sequence-level reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence decomposes into a chunk-level reverse-KL term and a future-potential term that captures the long-horizon effect of the current action. DriftOPD optimizes these two terms using a one-step drifting objective and a Q-function critic learned from offline demonstrations, respectively, enabling sequence-level optimization with only offline data and one-step action generation. Across multiple VLA architectures in simulation and real-world manipulation, DriftOPD generally outperforms existing one-step distillation baselines while achieving task success performance comparable to multi-step teacher policies. These results demonstrate that long-horizon behavior can be effectively distilled into one-step VLA action experts without online interaction or a separate teacher.

papers.title: МОДИФІКАЦІЯ НЕЙРОМЕРЕЖЕВОГО МЕТОДУ SPINN ДЛЯ НАБЛИЖЕНОГО РОЗВ'ЯЗАННЯ МІШАНОЇ ЗАДАЧІ ДЛЯ РІВНЯННЯ ТЕПЛОПРОВІДНОСТІ В ЕЛІПТИЧНІЙ ОБЛАСТІ
papers.abstract: Background. Parabolic differential equations are mathematical models in engineering designed to study wide range of applied models. This necessitates the development of approximate methods for solving them. Classical numerical methods based on finite difference and finite elements are difficult to apply to non-rectangular geometries of the domain and to high-dimensional domains. This becomes a problem even in the two-dimensional case. Neural networks methods, such as the Physics-informed neural network (PINN), can be applied to problems with complex domain geometry, but they still suffer from the problem of increasing domain dimension. Objective. Develop a modified approach based on Separable PINN (SPINN) for the approximate solution of a mixed problem for the heat conduction equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions in an elliptical domain. Methods. Application of the SPINN method after first converting the boundary value problem to a cylindrical coordinate system and applying modifications to the loss function and the point generation method to avoid problems associated with the singularity at zero in the Laplace operator in polar coordinates. Results. A modification of the SPINN method has been developed for the approximate solution of a mixed problem for the heat conduction equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions in an elliptical domain. The proposed approach is demonstrated on examples alongside the finite difference method and the PINN method to compare the results obtained. In each case, SPINN demonstrated lower relative errors and shorter computation times compared to both the finite difference method and the PINN method. Conclusions. The described application of the SPINN architecture to solving a mixed problem for the heat conduction equation allows for the optimization of engineering modeling of thermophysical processes in elliptical-shaped plates. The developed modification of the SPINN method demonstrated, through examples, better relative error values (1.25 times smaller in the first example and 1.15 times smaller in the second) with significantly shorter computation times (5 times shorter in the first example and 2 times shorter in the second) compared to PINN. Compared to the finite difference method, the difference is even more noticeable. This result confirms the effectiveness of the method and opens prospects for its further application to boundary value problems in curvilinear domains with arbitrary smooth boundaries.

papers.title: Research progress on generation and evolution mechanism of arc fault in aviation
papers.abstract: A significant hazard to the operational safety of aircraft is presented by aviation arcing faults, which constitute a critical safety challenge to be overcome, particularly for all-electric and more-electric aircraft variants. Given that aviation arcing faults are influenced by a multitude of factors, a summary of the mechanisms governing their generation and evolution is presented herein. Firstly, the formation and evolution mechanisms are analyzed from the perspective of individual electrical, electrode, and environmental factors. A systematic summary is provided of the principles by which electrical factors (power supply voltage, system current, power supply frequency and load type), electrode factors (vibration, relative velocity, electrode material), and environmental factors (barometric pressure, temperature, humidity, and salt spray) contribute to the initiation and sustainment of an arc. Secondly, the analysis is extended to the complex mechanisms that govern the generation and evolution of arcing faults under the coupled effects of dual, triple, and multiple factors. A deeper insight is thereby provided into the developmental patterns of dual-factor coupling (electrical-electrode, electrode-environmental and electrical-environmental); the key mechanisms by which arc evolution is influenced under triple-factor coupling (electrical-electrode-environmental); as well as the dynamic characteristics, energy transfer mechanisms, and damage mechanisms under multi-factor coupling conditions. Based upon the analysis, future research directions are outlined. It is proposed that a dual approach must be adopted. Firstly, the comprehensive quantitative studies on the effects of varying voltage, load, vibration, material, and environmental factors on arc characteristics be conducted. Secondly, the in-depth empirical multi-factor coupling investigations and triple-factor experiments also be undertaken. It is furthermore advocated that multi-scale models would be developed, which should then be calibrated with experimental data and subjected to uncertainty quantification, with the aim of enhancing predictive accuracy and refining protective strategies.

papers.title: A machine learning enhanced substructure method for full scale topology optimization of piezoelectric graded lattice structure
papers.abstract: Owing to their ultra-light weight, high compliance, and superior fracture resistance, piezoelectric graded lattice structures hold significant engineering potential for electromechanical devices. However, the three-dimensional (3D) full-scale topology optimization of such structures is severely hindered by the prohibitive computational costs of electromechanical coupling analysis. To address the issue, this paper proposes a machine learning (ML)-accelerated scheme for the large-scale explicit topology optimization of piezoelectric graded lattice structures. By integrating the 3D moving morphable components (MMC) approach with the partitioned coordinate mapping (PCM), this scheme achieves precise geometric construction of lattice skeletons. To overcome the computational bottleneck, a ML-accelerated scheme for the prediction of numerical shape function is developed, complemented by a physical residual-driven online correction strategy to tackle the degradation of the generalization at discontinuous 0/1 topological boundaries. Numerical validations demonstrate that the scheme drastically enhances computational efficiency while preserving global finite element analysis accuracy. Notably, computation time for a one-million degree-of-freedom (DOF) structure is reduced from 981.01 to 6.91 s. The developed approach is validated through three 3D full-scale numerical examples, including a cantilever beam, a cantilever plate, and an enclosed cylindrical energy harvester. Optimization results demonstrate that this scheme for electromechanical coupling problems is highly efficient and robust, effectively driving topology reconstruction to suppress local charge cancellation effects. Consequently, the final energy conversion rate is enhanced by up to 1.56 times over the initial configuration. Furthermore, comparisons confirm that these lattice structures yield higher absolute electrical energy output than conventional dense solid designs, which highlights their anticipated values in the applications in environmental energy harvesting.

papers.title: Mechanical and mass-transport design of hybrid TPMS-based metamaterial scaffold for orthopedic implants
papers.abstract: Orthopedic implants have been widely used to treat massive bone defects in clinical applications. To realize physiological functions after implanting, the mechanical and mass-transport properties of the designed implants should match the properties of the human skeleton. Additive-manufactured titanium lattice scaffolds have aroused great attention due to their superior performances, which can be precisely tuned via cellular structure design. Titanium alloys also show good biocompatibility, which is essential for implants. However, it is still challenging to concurrently design the mechanical and mass-transport properties of metamaterial-infilled implants, which are both of great importance in clinical usage. In this work, a novel series of hybrid triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS)-based lattice unit cells were proposed based on Boolean operations, in which the modulus and permeability can be precisely tuned by adjusting the cellular geometric parameters. The mechanical and mass-transport properties were evaluated numerically, and mechanical experiments were conducted to verify the finite element results. Response surface models of the cellular properties were established based on finite element analysis results to describe influence of geometric parameters, and feasible domains of the geometric parameters for implant design were also calculated. Cell culturing tests were also performed to validate the biocompatibility of the additive-manufactured lattice scaffolds. The proposed hybrid TPMS structure decoupled cellular stiffness from permeability and broadened the accessible design space of TPMS-based microstructure. This work paves the way for the design and clinical application of additive-manufactured metamaterial-infilled orthopedic implants. The results indicated that the proposed hybrid TPMS cells possess great potential for the design of orthopedic implants.

papers.title: Effect of UV Photo functionalization on Osseointegration of Titanium and Zirconia Dental Implants: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: Introduction:Dental implants are widely used for the replacement of missing teeth because of their predictable osseointegration and long-term clinical success. However, delayed osseointegration and early implant failure remain important clinical challenges. UV photofunctionalization has emerged as a surface-treatment approach that can improve implant surface hydrophilicity, reduce hydrocarbon contamination, and enhance osteogenic responses. Although substantial evidence exists for titanium implants, the quantitative evidence regarding UV-treated zirconia implants remains comparatively limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis therefore focused on the effects of UV photofunctionalization on titanium and zirconia dental implants. Objectives:To systematically evaluate and quantitatively compare the effects of UV photofunctionalization on the osseointegration of titanium and zirconia dental implants, with particular emphasis on bone-to-implant contact (BIC), implant stability quotient (ISQ), removal torque, and marginal bone loss (MBL). Methods:A PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted using studies evaluating UV-treated and non-treated titanium and zirconia implants. Clinical, animal, and experimental studies were considered. Data were extracted for BIC, ISQ, removal torque, and MBL. Mean difference (MD) was used for outcomes measured on the same scale, while standardized mean difference (SMD) was applied where different measurement scales were used. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic, and random-effects models were applied to account for variation in UV exposure, implant surface characteristics, and healing periods. A total of 26 studies were included in the quantitative synthesis. Results:UV photofunctionalization was associated with improved osseointegration-related outcomes for both titanium and zirconia implants. BIC increased by 17.8% for titanium and 16.3% for zirconia implants, with an overall pooled improvement of 17.1%. ISQ increased by 8.5 units for titanium and 6.9 units for zirconia implants, with a pooled improvement of 7.8 units. Removal torque increased by 10.1 Ncm for titanium and 8.2 Ncm for zirconia implants, with an overall pooled improvement of 9.2 Ncm. Marginal bone loss was reduced by 0.64 mm for titanium and 0.53 mm for zirconia implants, with an overall reduction of 0.58 mm. Moderate heterogeneity was observed, with I² values ranging from approximately 47% to 52% for marginal bone loss and approximately 49% overall. Conclusions:UV photofunctionalization was associated with improved biological and mechanical indicators of osseointegration in both titanium and zirconia dental implants. The findings indicate improvements in BIC, ISQ, and removal torque together with reduced marginal bone loss following UV treatment. However, the available evidence was heterogeneous, particularly regarding implant materials, UV exposure protocols, surface characteristics, and healing periods. Further standardized clinical studies with longer follow-up are required, particularly to strengthen the evidence for UV-photofunctionalized zirconia implants.

papers.title: Multi-field coupled optimization of an air-purifying BIPVT system with thermal–UV synergistic disinfection: A CFD–Bayesian optimization approach
papers.abstract: The use of renewable energy to reduce building energy consumption has become a major trend, while indoor bioaerosol control has received increasing attention in the post-pandemic era. Air-purifying building-integrated photovoltaic/thermal (BIPVT) systems utilize solar energy to simultaneously generate electricity, provide space heating, and purify indoor air. In this study, a thermal–UV synergistic inactivation mechanism is introduced to enhance the bioaerosol control capability of such systems. However, the highly non-uniform temperature, UV radiation, and flow fields, together with multi-dimensional structural parameters, make the coordinated optimization of power generation, heating, and air purification challenging. To address this issue, Bayesian optimization is introduced into BIPVT system optimization through a coupled CFD–Bayesian optimization framework. The results show that: 1. Bayesian optimization rapidly identified high-value regions within the first 20 iterations and increased the optimal scalarized utility to 2.068, representing a 19% improvement. 2. Under equal weighting of heat gain, power generation, and air purification, high-value designs were mainly associated with moderate PV coverage and upper-channel UV lamp placement. 3. Compared with random and uniform sampling, Bayesian optimization achieved 5.1% and 15.6% higher optimal scalarized utilities under comparable sample sizes. 4. Parametric analysis further confirmed its stability and effectiveness under different UV wavelengths, channel depths, and lamp numbers, while increasing UV lamps showed limited marginal benefits beyond two lamps. The results provide insights for controlling indoor airborne disease and offer a new approach for optimizing BIPVT systems.

papers.title: Probabilistic corrosion prediction of marine steel under future climate change scenarios using physics-informed Gaussian process regression
papers.abstract: Abstract This study proposes a framework of corrosion prediction by utilizing physics-informed Gaussian process regression (PI-GPR) and future climate change simulation. Long-term corrosion prediction of marine steel structures is routinely based on stationary environmental assumptions; however, future sea surface temperature (SST) changes should be taken into account as it may affect corrosion degradation over structural service life. The present work develops a probabilistic corrosion prediction based on the PI-GPR model, which is coupled with CMIP6-based SST projections. The proposed PI-GPR model incorporates a physics-based corrosion mean function into a probabilistic machine learning framework, enabling physically consistent long-term extrapolation with 95% credible intervals. Annual SST projections from 31 CMIP6 models under SSP126 and SSP585 were processed using a multi-model ensemble approach and applied to the seas surrounding the Korean Peninsula. The results demonstrate that scenario-based corrosion loss exceeds fixed-temperature estimates, with the deviation increasing over multi-decadal exposure. Especially, the West Sea exhibited the largest climate-induced corrosion deviation under SSP585, indicating strong regional sensitivity. These findings suggest that future SST trajectories should be considered as essential inputs for corrosion allowance, inspection planning, and reliability assessment of marine steel structures under climate change.

papers.title: Design, Manufacturing, and Testing of a Continuous Passive Motion Transmission Mechanism
papers.abstract: In this study, we present the development of a smart, dual-axis continuous passive motion (CPM) rehabilitation device for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty.Most commercial CPM systems provide only uniaxial flexion-extension motion, limiting their application in comprehensive hip rehabilitation.The proposed system introduces an additional abduction mechanism to enable multidirectional movement during postoperative recovery.The mechanical structure adopts a modular design that allows an independent assembly of the flexion and abduction modules.A programmable logic controller (PLC)-based electrical control unit integrated with a human-machine interface (HMI) was developed for coordinated dual-axis operation.Four endpoint position sensors were installed at the 0 and 90° limits of the flexion module and the 0 and 30° limits of the abduction module.Intermediate positions are controlled by the PLC according to the stepper-motor pulse count and linear-actuator stroke, while the endpoint position sensors provide origin confirmation, travel-limit detection, and overtravel protection.Under abnormal overtravel conditions, the PLC stops the corresponding motion and displays a warning on the HMI.Functional testing confirmed smooth and stable dual-axis operation.These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system and indicate greater motion versatility and integrated control functionality than conventional single-axis CPM configurations, supporting its potential for future clinical application.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence algorithms for complex industrial optimization
papers.abstract: We organize the research needs around three connected challenges: AI-assisted problem formulation and structural representation; scalable optimization of coupled resources and supply chains; and closed-loop adaptation in dynamic, uncertain, and multi-objective environments. Two requirements cut across all three challenges: structure-aware integration of optimization, learning, and simulation; and operational validation, human-AI collaboration, and accountability. In the latter, information, tasks, and decision authority are allocated among domain experts, operators, AI assistants and agents, optimizers, and simulators according to risk and context (Karapanagiotis et al., 2025).Industrial optimization begins before a solver is selected. Relevant information is distributed across data systems, engineering documents, regulations, and expert practice. These sources differ in timing, vocabulary, and reliability. Model formulation requires identification of the decisions, objectives, constraints, uncertainties, and couplings that define the operational problem. Translating an agreed description into equations is only one part of that task.Methods for constraint acquisition can infer candidate rules from examples and expert queries (Bessiere et al., 2017), while decision-focused approaches can optimize predictive models for downstream decision quality (Donti et al., 2017;Wilder et al., 2019). Rules inferred from data or text remain provisional until they are checked against actual operations. Each candidate rule requires verification of its provenance, scope, conflicts with other rules, and operational consequences before it enters a decision model. Human skills, decision rights, and handoff responsibilities may themselves be part of the modeled structure, particularly when tasks can move between people and automated components (Karapanagiotis et al., 2025).Large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents can mediate between informal descriptions and formal optimization models. They can propose formulations, generate solver code, and assign modeling or verification tasks to specialized components (Zhang et al., 2024a;Xiao et al., 2024;Yang et al., 2026). Recent work that combines LLM-based extraction with reusable modeling graphs and expert-defined templates illustrates a more controlled division of responsibility (Li et al., 2026). These outputs remain candidate models. Solver execution can expose coding errors or infeasibility, but it cannot establish semantic completeness or show that an omitted business rule is inconsequential.A traceable modeling loop records how constraints are acquired and classified, who validates them, how uncertainty and problem structure are represented, and when operational change triggers model revision. If the resulting problem is infeasible, the algorithm needs to identify the conflicting assumptions and return either an interpretable relaxation or a safe recovery action. Evaluation then turns on downstream decision performance under missing or changing information; fluent model generation alone is insufficient.The computational burden of large industrial optimization problems arises from both problem size and coordination across resources, organizations, and time scales. Machines, workforce capabilities, energy supply, inventory, and transport capacity are coupled through shared constraints, but their influence on system performance is unequal and state dependent. A disruption can shift the bottleneck from equipment to technicians, spare parts, storage, or transport. Algorithms need representations and sensitivity measures that identify the binding couplings and detect when those relationships change.In distributed scheduling, job-to-factory assignment and within-factory sequencing are interdependent (Naderi and Ruiz, 2010). Across a supply chain, procurement, production, inventory, and delivery decisions are made over different planning horizons. Solving these stages separately can shift costs, delays, or emissions downstream; even under restricted assumptions, integrated production-inventory-delivery models are computationally demanding (Gen et al., 2008;Li et al., 2017). Coordination also involves organizations, human planners, and AI agents that hold different information and decision rights. Recent supply-chain research on agentic AI accordingly treats human-agent roles and organizational constraints as design choices rather than assuming full autonomy (Trifone et al., 2026).Decomposition and mathematical programming can exploit sparsity and explicit constraint structure, while evolutionary algorithms and large-neighborhood search can explore difficult discrete and nonconvex search spaces (Yu and Gen, 2010;Pisinger and Ropke, 2010). A central design question is how to balance global exploration with local improvement. Global moves reallocate orders, capacity, and supply-chain flows; local moves refine sequences, routes, and maintenance schedules. Learned components may select neighborhoods, warm starts, decompositions, or algorithm configurations. Their value depends on preserving global consistency while reducing end-to-end decision time and resource use. A learned policy may improve one subproblem yet render another infeasible when cross-stage constraints are omitted, represented too coarsely, or invalidated by a disruption. Learned guidance also needs to recognize when a fixed decomposition is no longer valid.Multiple objectives introduce an additional tension between computational efficiency and decision effectiveness. Efficiency concerns whether an algorithm returns an answer before the decision deadline. Effectiveness covers feasibility, solution-set quality and diversity, and alignment with decision-maker preferences (Deb et al., 2002;Zhang et al., 2024b). Automated program search can generate heuristics and search rules, including variants for multi-objective optimization (Romera-Paredes et al., 2024;Yao et al., 2025). Their performance remains uncertain when the evaluation function overlooks cross-stage couplings. Evaluation should establish whether local gains persist once supply-chain interactions are accounted for and whether a globally consistent plan can be produced on time.Demand, resource availability, prices, and customer priorities change over different time scales. Parameter uncertainty, observed disruptions, distribution shift, and structural change each call for a different response. Repeatedly running a static optimizer after every event does not by itself create a closed-loop strategy.A closed-loop algorithm links state estimation and prediction to model revision, optimization, execution, and feedback. Robust planning and reactive rescheduling play complementary roles and can be coordinated through rolling-horizon optimization, online learning, dynamic optimization, and calibrated simulation. Full regeneration may improve the objective value but increase schedule nervousness; local repair preserves stability but can lock in a poor global allocation (Vieira et al., 2003;Blackburn et al., 1986). Reinforcement learning can represent delayed consequences, but exploration in industrial systems must respect constraints during training and deployment. A high expected return does not establish acceptable tail risk or recoverability (García and Fernández, 2015;Wachi et al., 2024). Recent dynamic-scheduling work shows how a formal supervisor can restrict reinforcement learning to a safe, non-blocking operating space and support rapid recovery after disruptions (Wang et al., 2026).Digital twins are useful for stress testing only if their models remain valid under the disruptions that drive decisions (Tao et al., 2019). Emerging architectures connect digital twins, multiple agents, online multi-objective optimization, and human-robot collaboration (Huang et al., 2026). These combinations strengthen the case for a closed loop, but they also increase the number of interfaces whose state, latency, and failure modes need monitoring.Priorities assigned to cost, service, sustainability, resilience, and workload may also change during a disruption. Adaptation therefore requires more than repeated static Pareto optimization. The algorithm needs to choose among continuing or repairing the current plan, re-optimizing, updating the model, and escalating the decision to a human decision-maker. Task and decision authority may also need to shift as risk, AI confidence, human workload, and time pressure change. Evaluation needs to report feasibility under distributional and structural shifts, tail-risk and recovery metrics, and operational gains net of excessive plan changes.Hybrid algorithmic architectures are justified only when their components perform distinct, necessary functions, their interfaces can be validated, and the integrated method outperforms a strong but simpler baseline (Fan et al., 2026;Wiberg et al., 2026). Learning can estimate uncertain states or surrogate models and select search controls when equivalent information is unavailable within the operational deadline. Mathematical and constraint programming can enforce explicit feasibility logic and provide bounds. Evolutionary algorithms are useful for discrete, nonconvex, black-box, or preference-sensitive search, whereas simulation represents behavior that is difficult to express analytically.The interfaces between components deserve equal scrutiny because they govern information exchange, uncertainty propagation, and failure detection. A learned initialization may accelerate a solver yet fail under distribution shift. Likewise, a high-fidelity simulation may consume the computation needed for adequate stress testing. Ablation studies need to test both individual contributions and failures at component interfaces under the same operational budget.A learning-based or generative component may propose a formulation or heuristic; a solver, simulator, or explicit checker can then test it. The inclusion of every added component should be justified by a verifiable improvement in decision quality. This division of responsibility is especially important for LLM-based agents, whose ability to orchestrate tools does not remove the need for formal checks and controlled access to operational systems.Operational reliability depends on how an algorithm interacts with enterprise data flows, shop-floor execution systems, and human decision-makers. Stale state information, interface mismatches, human overrides, and execution deviations can all change the optimization problem. Monitoring, rollback, reoptimization, escalation, and revalidation are consequently part of the algorithm lifecycle.The appropriate unit of analysis is the hybrid decision team rather than the AI component in isolation.Its performance depends on how information, tasks, and authority are distributed among operators, managers, AI agents, optimization solvers, and organizational units. Human participants can contribute tacit knowledge and handle exceptions, but poor handoffs or unclear authority can delay responses and obscure accountability. Experimental evidence from AI-assisted production indicates that team organization affects failure recovery through the frequency and quality of communication (Krzywdzinski et al., 2026). Semantic models for dynamic work sharing offer one way to represent changing human and artificial roles, although their contribution must ultimately be tested through team and system outcomes (Karapanagiotis et al., 2025).Accordingly, evaluation should include communication quality, handoff latency, calibrated reliance, intervention workload, recovery performance, and operational outcomes alongside conventional algorithmic metrics. Explanations need separate scrutiny: in a job-shop scheduling experiment, brief AI rationales increased behavioral reliance without necessarily improving understanding (Saßmannshausen et al., 2026). Trust, reliance, and decision correctness are distinct measures.Claims of improvement require comparison against competitive optimization, learning, and engineering baselines under matched end-to-end resource budgets. Those budgets include data preparation, model development, computation, simulation, and human effort. Experiments need to vary coupling strength, constraint tightness, disruption severity, distribution shift, and decision deadlines rather than instance size alone. Studies should also report prediction quality, optimization quality, and operational value separately. Optimization quality includes feasibility, optimality gap, regret, and Pareto-front approximation quality; operational value includes plan stability, service performance, recovery time, and integration effort.Fluent formulations and executable code do not establish correctness. Grounded in solver functions, LLM interfaces can nevertheless support infeasibility diagnosis, sensitivity analysis, and what-if or why-not queries (Chen et al., 2025). High-consequence decisions still require traceable constraints, validated alternatives, controlled system access, and explicit human authority over rollback and escalation.The three challenges span problem formulation and structural representation, scalable optimization of coupled resources and supply chains, and closed-loop adaptation. Success depends on a faithful operational model, coordination of coupled decisions within the available time, and revision of those decisions without sacrificing feasibility or stability. Structure-aware integration determines whether the algorithmic components work together; operational validation, human-AI collaboration, and accountability determine whether gains at one stage translate into system-level performance.Prediction accuracy, average reward, isolated benchmark gains, and the addition of another AI component provide incomplete evidence of progress. The stronger standard is better decision quality under realistic constraints, coupling, and change, together with communication and authority arrangements that support timely intervention and recovery. Ultimately, an industrial AI algorithm needs to solve the right problem within the decision deadline and continue to produce feasible, stable, and controllable decisions as operating conditions change.

papers.title: Systematic Literature Review of AI-Powered Computing and Digital Transformation from the Standpoint of Flipped Classrooms and Blended Learning for Higher Education
papers.abstract: At the core of Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0) evolution is digital transformation, a process that goes beyond merely adopting digital tools to fundamentally restructuring institutional workflows, pedagogical methodologies, and student engagement models. Concurrently, the maturity of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered computing-encompassing machine learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and computer vision-has provided the technological infrastructure necessary to realize highly personalized, scalable, and data-driven educational frameworks. Traditional, lecture-heavy instructional models are increasingly proving inadequate for developing the critical thinking, problem-solving, and lifelonglearning competencies required in the modern workforce. Consequently, learner-centric pedagogical frameworks have gained significant traction. Among these, the flipped classroom model and blended learning environments stand out as premier strategies for optimizing higher education. The flipped classroom model inverts traditional instruction by delivering informational content outside of class hours (often via digital media), thereby freeing up synchronous class time for active, collaborative, and experiential learning. Blended learning broadens this scope by systematically integrating face-to-face instruction with online learning, creating a flexible, cohesive and multimodal educational experience. While the individual merits of AI-powered computing, digital transformation, flippedclassrooms, and blended learning are extensively documented, their intersection remains fragmented in current literature. Higher education institutions frequently deploy advanced AI tools without aligning them with active learning taxonomies, or conversely, design blended curricula that fail to leverage the computational power of modern AI infrastructure. This Systematic Literature Review(SLR) addresses this critical gap by synthesizing global research from the past decade, this study investigates how AI-powered computing acts as a catalyst for digital transformation specifically through the lens of flipped and blended learning environments in higher education.

papers.title: AI-Based Control of Differential Vacuum in the MuVacAS Prototype for IFMIF–DONES Particle Accelerator
papers.abstract: Developing materials capable of withstanding extreme irradiation is a fundamental challenge for realizing nuclear fusion as a sustainable energy source. The IFMIF–DONES facility, currently under construction, will address this need by producing a fusion-relevant neutron flux using a high-power deuteron beam striking a flowing lithium target, enabling accelerated qualification of candidate structural materials. Validating the accelerator and target technologies requires precise control of the ultra-high-vacuum region near the lithium surface, yet direct pressure sensing in this irradiated zone is challenging and conventional controllers can struggle with the associated nonlinear gas-flow dynamics. As part of the DONES–FLUX project, this work introduces a data-driven workflow for indirect pressure estimation and autonomous regulation in the MuVacAS prototype, a dedicated experimental platform that reproduces the final beamline section of IFMIF–DONES. Two Fourier Neural Operator surrogate models are learned from real data: one serves as a virtual sensor to infer chamber pressure from upstream readings, while the other models system dynamics to provide a safe, fast training environment for a Deep Reinforcement Learning controller. The trained agent uses virtual-sensor feedback during deployment and reliably regulates argon injection across operating scenarios, including conditions not seen during training. Experimental campaigns show that the RL-based controller yields promising control results, achieving stable regulation without manual retuning. These results demonstrate a viable pathway for deploying advanced learning-based control in fusion-relevant accelerator systems, supporting the operational readiness of IFMIF–DONES and future fusion technology infrastructures.

papers.title: PhyRL-PINN: Full-scale adaptive physics-informed ship sideslip estimation via reinforcement-learning-guided parameter scheduling
papers.abstract: Estimating a navigation-derived proxy of the ground-referenced ship sideslip angle under real-sea conditions requires combining physical structure with data-driven flexibility. PhyRL-PINN is a physics-informed residual-regularized neural estimator with reinforcement-learning-guided coefficient scheduling. A reduced-order lateral-dynamics prior is retained, while an actor–critic scheduler infers regularized equivalent structural coefficients from causal measurement histories. Within each 12-s window, six coefficient vectors are inferred at consecutive 2-s subinterval endpoints for endpoint-conditioned physical reconstruction, whose terminal state conditions the final estimate. Training and evaluation are performed offline on recorded measurements. The supervisory target, reconstructed from GNSS/INS speed over ground, course over ground, and heading, is a ground-referenced sideslip proxy rather than a direct water-relative hydrodynamic measurement. Using 59 voyages, 40,830 s of operation, and 163,379 synchronized samples, PhyRL-PINN achieves an RMSE of 1.74 × 1 0 − 3 rad and an R 2 of 0.9911 under seen-voyage blockwise interpolation, corresponding to RMSE reductions of approximately 78% and 60% relative to TimeMixer and MMAE, respectively. Under five-fold voyage-level grouped cross-validation, it retains an R 2 of 0.9341 on held-out voyages. Ablation results confirm the contributions of physics-residual regularization and state-dependent coefficient scheduling.

papers.title: Autonomous Robot Networks for Infrastructure Inspection: A Literature-informed Conceptual Framework for Predictive Monitoring, Asset-specific Adaptation, and Safety Assurance
papers.abstract: Aging infrastructure systems, including bridges, roads, tunnels, pipelines, substations, and utility corridors, present growing inspection and maintenance challenges for public agencies and asset owners, particularly under conditions of deferred maintenance, aging assets, and constrained renewal budgets (American Society of Civil Engineers, 2021; World Bank, 2020). Conventional inspection workflows rely heavily on manual fieldwork, periodic surveys, and fragmented reporting practices, which can limit inspection frequency, increase operational exposure, and reduce consistency across distributed asset portfolios (Federal Highway Administration, 2022; ISO 55000, 2014; ISO 55001, 2014). Although robotics, sensing, computer vision, digital twins, and predictive analytics have advanced substantially, research in these areas remains fragmented across platforms, sensing modalities, and asset domains (Koch et al., 2015; Spencer et al., 2019; Jiang et al., 2021; Opoku et al., 2021).This paper presents a literature-informed conceptual framework for an autonomous multi-robot inspection network intended to support predictive monitoring and maintenance prioritization. The framework was developed through a structured conceptual synthesis of prior research spanning multiple infrastructure and technical domains. It distinguishes invariant cross-domain architectural components from asset-specific adaptation requirements for bridges, roads, tunnels, pipelines, substations, and utility corridors. The proposed architecture integrates heterogeneous robotic agents, multimodal sensing, coordinated mission planning, defect detection, condition estimation, confidence-aware digital twin updating, maintenance prioritization, explainable reporting, and safety assurance within a unified decision-support structure (Gerkey & Mataric, 2004; Parker, 2008; Hall & Llinas, 1997; Khaleghi et al., 2013; Sacks et al., 2020; Jiang et al., 2021; Jardine et al., 2006; Doshi-Velez & Kim, 2017; NIST, 2023). This integration is literature-informed at the level of recurring functional requirements reported across robotics, multisensor fusion, digital twin, predictive maintenance, and trustworthy-AI research, while the specific cross-domain architectural composition presented here is proposed by the authors as a conceptual synthesis.The paper makes five contributions. First, it presents a structured framework-development approach that uses prior literature to identify recurring operational and technical requirements relevant to autonomous infrastructure inspection. Second, it defines a layered architecture that separates common system functions from asset-specific sensing, mobility, defect classification, safety, and maintenance adaptations. Third, it formalizes the system model by specifying variables, normalization logic, weighting structures, thresholds, and uncertainty pathways relevant to maintenance-priority outputs. The need to distinguish defect detection, condition estimation, prognosis, uncertainty handling, and maintenance prioritization is supported by prior condition-monitoring and predictive-maintenance literature, whereas the particular variables, weighting logic, aggregation equations, and threshold structures are author-proposed for conceptual operationalization in this framework. These variables and formal decision structures are proposed by the authors as a conceptual operationalization informed by prior literature rather than adopted directly from a single source. Fourth, it introduces a safety-assurance structure addressing hazards, fail-safe states, communication loss, geofencing, collision avoidance, hardware and battery faults, human takeover, change control, and incident reporting, drawing on prior work on human oversight, trustworthy AI, cyber-physical risk, and governance while proposing an integrated inspection-specific control structure for this domain (Parasuraman et al., 2000; Sheridan, 2016; Endsley, 2017; European Commission High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence, 2019; Humayed et al., 2017; NIST, 2023; NIST, 2024). Prior literature supports the need for human oversight, bounded autonomy, traceability, and risk-governed deployment, while the inspection-specific integration of these controls into a unified governance structure is proposed by the authors. Fifth, it outlines a prospective validation strategy with explicit hypotheses, baseline comparisons, external-site expectations, stress testing, and failure-case reporting.This study is conceptual and design-oriented; it does not present field-validated performance results or claim empirical superiority over existing inspection workflows. Instead, it offers an integrated foundation for future prototyping, pilot deployment, and comparative evaluation of autonomous multi-robot inspection systems in infrastructure management.

papers.title: Simultaneous strength-ductility enhancement and damping capacity regulation in a non-equiatomic FeMnCoNi multi-principal-element alloy produced via laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: In this study, a Fe 50 Mn 20 Ni 20 Co 10 multi-principal-element alloy (MPEA) containing 0.2 at% Al was fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). Two processing conditions, i.e., a low-power, low-speed regime and a high-power, high-speed regime, were compared within the optimal volumetric energy density (VED) window. The low-power, low-speed process prolongs melt pool lifetime. It triggers explosive nucleation of Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles, yielding a high-volume fraction of finely dispersed precipitates, a chessboard-like microstructure, and a well-developed geometrically necessary dislocation substructure. The high-power, high-speed process with short melt-pool residence produces only sparse, coarse oxides and a loose dislocation configuration. These microstructural differences lead to pronounced property divergence. Owing to strong Orowan and dislocation strengthening from the dense nanoparticles, the low-power, low-speed specimen achieves a yield strength of 585 MPa and uniform elongation of 18.3%, exhibiting strength-ductility synergy with microvoid coalescence fracture. The high-power, high-speed specimen shows only 410 MPa yield strength, 10.3% uniform elongation, and mixed quasi-cleavage fracture. Damping behavior follows an opposite trend, revealing a fundamental trade-off: the same dense nanoparticles and dislocation networks that provide strong strengthening and high strength-ductility synergy also act as strong pinning sites that suppress dislocation mobility, keeping tan δ as low as ~0.012 in the low-power, low-speed specimen, while weaker pinning in the high-power, high-speed specimen gives tan δ of 0.023. This work reveals this trade-off and a mechanism for synergistic optimization of strength, ductility, and damping by tailoring nanoprecipitate characteristics and dislocation configurations via thermal history, offering a basis for integrated process-microstructure-property design in additively manufactured MPEAs.

papers.title: Generative design of high-fidelity microstructures using physics-aware machine learning
papers.abstract: Generative models are increasingly being applied in materials science to enable materials design. However, generating out-of-distribution microstructures with high fidelity that satisfy multiple target properties remains a major challenge. Here, we present a physics-aware generative-optimization strategy for the inverse design of microstructures, guided by mutually exclusive properties. The approach integrates interfacial and crystallographic information directly into the loss function of surrogate models, together with introducing a latent-space sampling scheme that balances microstructural diversity with physical realizability. We demonstrate the framework using a small yet diverse alloy dataset comprising well-characterized microstructures and tensile stress-strain responses. By targeting strength-ductility synergy, the generated out-of-distribution microstructures exhibit substantially improved fidelity, particularly in their interfacial features. The produced microstructures are validated by crystal plasticity finite element simulations and experiments. We attribute the enhanced mechanical performance to the emergence of a bimodal grain-size morphology absent from the training data. Our results demonstrate a data-efficient strategy for high-fidelity microstructure design that leverages interfacial physics to achieve multiple properties synergy. This study uses physics-aware AI to generate high-fidelity microstructures beyond existing data distributions, resulting in a bimodal grain structure that enables improved strength and ductility.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Mining and Metallurgy: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Mapping of Research Trends
papers.abstract: Mining and metallurgy are increasingly influenced by growing demand for critical metals, digitalization, and the transition toward sustainable and circular production systems. This study aimed to map recent advances, dominant research themes, methodological trends, and knowledge gaps across the interconnected fields of mining and metallurgy. A systematic literature review following the PRISMA 2020 framework was combined with bibliometric analysis and keyword mapping using VOSviewer. The review analyzed 55 Scopus-indexed open-access articles published between 2025 and 2026 across three journals. Five thematic clusters were identified: physical metallurgy, alloy engineering, and manufacturing; extractive metallurgy and hydrometallurgy; mineral processing, geochemistry, and deposit exploration; mining engineering, geotechnics, and safety; and artificial intelligence, automation, and process digitalization. Experimental characterization integrated with modelling emerged as the dominant research approach, while waste valorization, critical metal recovery, continuous monitoring, and artificial intelligence represented prominent research trends. However, the literature remained fragmented, with limited integration among extraction processes, materials design, environmental assessment, and industrial process control. Many automation and machine-learning applications were also validated primarily through laboratory-scale experiments or simulations. This study concludes that future development requires industrial-scale validation, life-cycle sustainability assessment, interoperable datasets, and cross-disciplinary digital twin frameworks that connect mineral extraction, metallurgical processing, and intelligent control systems to support more sustainable, efficient, and resilient resource production worldwide.

papers.title: Digitalization in Industrial Facilities and the Classification of Maintenance Types: A Review
papers.abstract: The digitalization of industrial facilities, driven by Industry 4.0 technologies, is fundamentally changing how production assets are monitored, modeled, and managed, and its strongest effect is felt in maintenance management, where traditional corrective and time-based practices are giving way to data-driven, condition-based, and predictive maintenance strategies. This review addresses two linked questions: how industrial maintenance types can be organized within a consistent framework, and how digital enablers such as cyber-physical systems, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), the digital twin, machine learning, and remaining-useful-life (RUL) estimation reshape these types. The study is designed as a narrative (non-systematic) review of seventy-one peer-reviewed journal articles published between 1995 and 2026, complemented by the primary sources of the reliability centered maintenance literature. Maintenance strategies are classified and compared along a reactiveproactive axis as corrective, planned/periodic, condition-based, predictive, reliability-centered (RCM), risk-based (RBM), and opportunistic maintenance. We show that digitalization repositions these types within a continuous condition-monitoring–diagnosis–prognosis–decision loop. The review also surveys recent developments (large language models and generative artificial intelligence, federated and edge learning, explainable AI, digital-twin interoperability standards, and the human-centric maintenance perspective of Industry 4.0) and discusses their implications for maintenance management. As an original contribution, we propose a conceptual digital-maintenance framework that couples the digital twin, RUL-based maintenance-interval computation, and an expected profit-loss indicator (ePLI) with a reminder/alarm decision layer; the ePLI is formalized through an expected-loss expression, a threshold-based reminder/alarm rule, and an illustrative application scenario. The findings indicate that digitalization turns maintenance types from mutually exclusive choices into elements of an integrated asset-management continuum, and that Industry 4.0 and trustworthy-AI research adds a human-centric dimension to this continuum. papers.title: Open-source framework for parametric study of hydrofoil profiles and motivation for using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN)
papers.abstract: This research presents a robust, automated, open-source computational framework for generating high throughput hydrodynamic datasets for Physics Informed Neural Network (PINN) applications. Recognising the significant computational overhead of conventional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) in parametric design spaces, this study proposes an integrated approach using GMSH for algorithmic mesh generation and OpenFOAM for high-fidelity fluid flow simulations. The framework is used to conduct an extensive parametric investigation on an HPC system for three distinct hydrofoil geometries: the NACA 0012, NACA 2412, and NACA 4412 profiles. Simulations are performed across a comprehensive operational envelope, covering angles of attack (α) from −15◦ to +15◦ and Reynolds numbers (Re) from 104 to 107. The resulting structured database contains spatial distributions of velocity and pressure fields, providing the empirical foundation for a deep learning architecture developed within the PyTorch ecosystem. To ensure physical consistency, the PINN architecture enforces the governing Navier Stokes equations by incorporating the conservation law residuals directly into the composite loss function. By automating the transition from geometric definition to numerical solution, the framework provides the necessary ground truth for training and validating PINNs. The accuracy of the surrogate model is evaluated by comparing the L2 relative error and pressure coefficient (Cp) distributions with OpenFOAM steady-state results. This approach aims to accelerate the prediction of hydrodynamic performance in foil-assisted vessel analysis while ensuring that the surrogate model strictly adheres to governing physical laws. The proposed methodology offers a scalable and accessible pathway for developing rapid-response surrogate models in maritime engineering.

papers.title: Home Energy Use Optimizer: A Review of IoT, AI, and Fault-Aware Residential Energy Management
papers.abstract: Residential electrification, connected appliances, and variable tariffs have increased the need for practical home energy management systems (HEMS). Existing research demonstrates the value of optimization, Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and model predictive control for reducing electricity cost and peak demand. However, many solutions emphasize scheduling and forecasting while treating appliance-level fault detection and automatic safety isolation as secondary functions. This paper presents a structured narrative review of 13 studies published between 2020 and 2026 and synthesizes their objectives, methods, strengths, and implementation gaps. Based on the synthesis, a low-cost Home Energy Use Optimizer is proposed using an ESP32/Arduino-class controller, voltage and current sensing, relay-based load isolation, local display, Wi-Fi connectivity, bill estimation, and user alerts. The architecture combines real-time monitoring, threshold-based protection, remote supervision, and extensibility toward predictive analytics. The paper identifies hardware validation, interoperable device integration, cybersecurity, explainable control, and field evaluation as priorities for future work.

papers.title: Adapting medical vision foundation models for volumetric medical image segmentation via active learning and selective semi-supervised fine-tuning
papers.abstract: Medical vision foundation models (Med-VFMs) have shown strong potential for medical image analysis by leveraging representations learned from large-scale self-supervised pre-training on unlabeled data. However, their performance and generalization remain limited in downstream tasks, particularly volumetric medical image segmentation. Although fine-tuning on labeled target-domain data improves performance, existing approaches typically rely on randomly selected samples, which may overlook informative data and hinder adaptation. To address this, we propose an Active Selective Semi-supervised Fine-tuning (ASSFT) framework for efficient adaptation of Med-VFMs to volumetric segmentation tasks. ASSFT integrates active learning with selective semi-supervised learning to maximize performance under limited annotation budgets without requiring source data. Specifically, we introduce an Active Test-Time Sample Query strategy that identifies informative target-domain samples using two complementary metrics: Diversified Knowledge Divergence (DKD) and Anatomical Segmentation Difficulty (ASD). DKD captures both the knowledge gap between pre-training and target domains and intra-domain diversity, enabling selection of samples containing novel and diverse information. ASD estimates segmentation difficulty by measuring predictive uncertainty in foreground regions, prioritizing anatomically complex cases over background-dominated samples. Furthermore, we propose a Selective Semi-supervised Fine-tuning strategy that leverages unlabeled data by incorporating only reliable pseudo-labeled samples based on predictive confidence and semantic proximity to labeled data, thereby mitigating noise. Extensive experiments on five volumetric segmentation tasks demonstrate that ASSFT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art active learning and domain adaptation methods while requiring substantially fewer annotations, highlighting its effectiveness, efficiency, and strong generalization capability.

papers.title: High-dynamic-range monitoring and 3D reconstruction of melt pool multi-physics fields and their relationships with formation quality in laser directed energy deposition
papers.abstract: In laser directed energy deposition (L-DED), strong radiation contrast, scarce reliable flow features, and insufficient microscale stereo-calibration accuracy remain major bottlenecks for melt pool multi-physics monitoring. Existing approaches are often limited to a single physical field or localized regions, hindering high-accuracy, high-dynamic-range (HDR) characterization of temperature, flow, and morphology fields, as well as the establishment of quantitative relationships between melt pool states and formation quality. To address these challenges, a single-camera HDR monitoring system is developed. A self-calibrated tri-band two-color pyrometry (ST-TP) method exploits intrinsic melt pool radiation features and complementary tri-band responses to achieve wide-range temperature measurement without additional registration targets. A dual-band fusion optical-flow tracking (DF-OFT) method integrates complementary thermal textures to reconstruct melt pool surface flow without external tracer particles. Combined with radiation-feature-based stereo matching, temporal tracking, 2D thermal-texture mapping, and a six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) calibration device, the framework enables synchronized 3D reconstruction of melt pool multi-physics fields. Experiments demonstrate a measurable temperature span approaching 2000 °C or higher, a temperature error below 1%, an increase of over 40% in effective measurement area, and a mean reconstruction error below 0.66%. Pearson analysis reveals strong relationships among process parameters, melt pool characteristics, and formation quality, with representative correlation magnitudes ranging from 0.76 to 0.99. EBSD analysis further links melt pool cooling behavior to Ti-6Al-4V microstructure, with higher cooling rates generally associated with finer α′ martensitic microstructures. These results demonstrate the potential of melt pool multi-physics information as quality-related process indicators for online quality assessment and closed-loop control in L-DED.

papers.title: A chance-constrained and constraint-aware reinforcement learning methodology for hydrogen-integrated energy systems under uncertainty
papers.abstract: Rapid growth of renewable resources and hydrogen infrastructure is reshaping multi-energy systems while amplifying operational uncertainty. This study introduces a decision-making structure for an electricity–heat–gas system with hydrogen production, storage, and refueling facilities, explicitly capturing variability in renewable output, electric-vehicle behavior, and hydrogen demand. A chance-constrained formulation governs interlinked energy flows and ensures probabilistic feasibility of network and equipment limits. To handle real-time operational adjustments, the model is paired with a constraint-aware reinforcement learning (RL) strategy that adapts to evolving conditions without violating safety or physical requirements. Hydrogen acts as a flexible carrier connecting power and gas networks via coordinated electrolysis and storage. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach enhances system reliability, alleviates hydrogen demand fluctuations, and reduces operating costs compared with deterministic scheduling, demonstrating its value for resilient hydrogen-integrated energy systems.

papers.title: The Boundary of Knowledge: A Framework for Learning the Limits of Identifiability in Artificial Intelligence Inference
papers.abstract: Predictive systems are typically trained to produce an answer for every query, even when the available evidence is compatible with more than one true state of the world. Existing safeguards against this failure mode largely act at the level of a single model's output distribution: calibration, selective prediction, and conformal prediction all summarize uncertainty as a scalar or a set derived from one fitted model, rather than asking whether the evidence could, in principle, ever determine the target. Separately, the causal-inference literature has long formalized identifiability—whether a query is a well-defined function of the available distribution—and has recently begun to study which additional experiments would tighten partial-identification bounds. These two literatures have developed largely independently, and neither, to the best of our knowledge, packages the result as an explicit, three-way, auditable classification (identifiable / conditionally identifiable / non-identifiable) with a machine-checkable ambiguity certificate that a downstream system can act on. We formalize this problem, introduce definitions that separate structural non-identifiability from model uncertainty, data uncertainty, and computational difficulty, and propose the Identifiability Boundary Framework (IBF): a fourteen-module architecture that represents competing explanations of the evidence as explicit “worlds,” certifies when two such worlds are observationally indistinguishable yet target-divergent, selects the minimum-cost additional observation or intervention that would separate them, and re-evaluates the boundary after acquisition. We give a formal problem statement, precise definitions, a minimum-information acquisition objective, and a full algorithm. We position the contribution carefully against the closest prior work—in particular recent work on ex-ante experiment selection for partial causal-effect identification—and are explicit that the individual mechanisms are not new in isolation; the contribution is a general, cross-domain formalization, an auditable certificate object, a sequential re-evaluation loop, and an evaluation protocol spanning causal, generative, and dynamical-system testbeds. We report a complete experimental design, baseline suite, metric set, and ablation plan; no results are claimed, and all reported numbers in this paper are explicitly marked as illustrative templates for the expected reporting format, not experimental findings.
